finding.claim: OS command injection: the unauthenticated /ping endpoint concatenates the req.query.host value into a shell command string passed to child_process.exec, which runs it through a shell. An attacker can append shell metacharacters (e.g. host=8.8.8.8;id or $(...)) to run arbitrary commands as the server user, and the output is returned in the response.
finding.source: req.query.host (HTTP GET query parameter on /ping, no authentication)

trace.note: req.query.host concatenated into shell command string and passed to exec()
command stdout reflected back to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No validation, allowlist, or escaping of host. No authentication or middleware on the app. exec uses a shell. Express may deliver an array or object for host, which makes concatenation worse but is not a guard. /version uses execFile with constant args and /uptime uses a constant command string, so both are safe and are not reported.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to shell-backed exec() with no validation, authentication or middleware (app defined at tools.js:4-6). Commands run anonymously, and stdout is returned at tools.js:11 whenever the final command exits 0, e.g. host=8.8.8.8;id.
